testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that the spring brakes come on automatically when:
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, the spring brakes should come on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, block the wheels and release air by pumping the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes engage.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are safe and work well for stopping large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is needed for:
questions.explanation: With few exceptions, you need a tank endorsement to transport liquids or gases. This includes both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: What is the air compressor connected to?
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine using gears or a belt.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both can damage the brakes by applying too much force.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol?

options.text: To stop the brakes from squeaking.
To prevent people from breathing the air.

questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It releases alcohol into the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning light is:

options.text: Not required on air brake vehicles.

questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning light. If it comes on while driving, stop the vehicle and have the system checked.

questions.question: What color are anti-lock brake malfunction lights?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have yellow warning lights that show when the system is not working.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks are in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. The number and size of tanks varies depending on the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if brakes get too hot?

options.text: The air compressor cools them down.

questions.explanation: When brakes overheat from heavy use, they can stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum safe air loss is 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that:

options.text: Turn on the low pressure warning light.
Turn off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pushing the brake pedal triggers an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Spring brakes come on when:

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a control on the dashboard is activated.
When the tires have minimal tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. When you see the low pressure warning signal, safely pull off the road and stop your vehicle right away.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes completely until the wheels lock up, release the brakes until the wheels start rolling, then repeat the process.
Apply the brakes about halfway, but allow the wheels to keep rolling.
Apply the brakes completely until the wheels lock up and the vehicle stops.
Apply the emergency brake until the vehicle starts to slow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes completely until the wheels lock up, release the brakes until the wheels start rolling, then repeat the process.
questions.explanation: The stab braking method involves fully applying the brakes until they lock. Then release them until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within:
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you press, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: What must be on an air tank in an air-braked vehicle?
questions.explanation: All air tanks in air-braked vehicles must have one-way check valves between the air compressor and the first reservoir. This stops air from leaking out.

questions.question: The ____ are turned on by an electric switch that is triggered by the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pushing the brake pedal triggers an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes
A part in the braking unit that lets air move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: The parking brake should be:

options.text: Used every time you park your vehicle
Set when driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Used every time you park your vehicle
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: A driver can rely on front wheel braking to work:
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well in all road conditions. Front wheel skids are very unlikely, even on ice.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Check that it is tight and in good condition.
